court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: V Additional Family Court, Chennai (O.P.No.3476 of 2008 and O.P.No.976 of 2010)
facts_of_case: The husband filed a petition for divorce in O.P.No.3476 of 2008 and the wife filed a petition for restitution of conjugal rights in O.P.No.976 of 2010. The trial court dismissed the husband's petition and allowed the wife's petition. The husband has appealed against these orders.

legal_principles.principle: The wife cannot be allowed to mark documents which have not been proved and tested by cross examination at the belated stage after the appellant/husband's counsel made his submissions.
legal_principles.held: The wife cannot be allowed to mark documents which have not been proved and tested by cross examination at the belated stage after the appellant/husband's counsel made his submissions.

legal_principles.principle: The conduct of the parties suggest that the matrimonial bond is beyond repair, the marriage would become sham and dejure declaration of dissolution of marriage is necessary.
legal_principles.held: The conduct of the parties suggest that the matrimonial bond is beyond repair, the marriage would become sham and dejure declaration of dissolution of marriage is necessary.
cited_cases: Naveen Kohli Vs. Neelu Kohli (2006) 1675 AIR SC
Samar Ghosh Vs. Jaya Ghosh (2007) 4 SCC 511
K. Srinivas Rao Vs. D.A. Deepa (2013) 5 SCC 226
Sukhendu Das Vs. Rita Mukherjee (2017) 9 SCC 632

outcome.final_order: The appeal is dismissed as the husband failed to establish cruelty by his wife.
